About this book

Shhh… the tablet is sleeping.

The Day the Tablet Slept is a funny 32-page picture book for ages 3–7, in paperback. Shhh… the tablet is sleeping. So what shall we do?

On Saturday morning, Ada zooms downstairs to find the family tablet snoring a teeny-tiny zzz-bip under a purple nightcap. It’s taking a day off. So Ada and her dog Biscuit make their own fun. They build a block tower (CRASH!), splash through every puddle (SPLOOOSH, all over Papa), turn a big empty box into the ADA-1 rocket and blast off past a planet made entirely of socks.

Children love to join in on the refrain, shout Biscuit’s WOOF!, and check on the sleepy tablet as it snoozes through the day. Short, rhythmic read-aloud pages and bold, full-bleed pictures make it a cozy bedtime book and a fun one to read again and again. The tablet is never the bad guy. It just needed a nap, and in the morning Ada can’t wait to tell it about her day.

At the back, grown-ups get ‘Talk about it’ questions, a ‘Plan your own Play Day’ page and a QR code for a free printable planner and coloring pages.

Pairs with 100 Screen-Free Plays as the Play Day bundle.

What you get

  • A funny bedtime story starring Ada, her dog Biscuit and a cardboard-box rocket, with a very sleepy tablet in a nightcap as the running joke
  • A read-aloud refrain (‘Shhh… the tablet is sleeping. So what shall we do?’) and a WOOF! for children to shout along to
  • Bold, full-bleed flat illustrations on every spread, with a warm, varied cast (Papa is the everyday grown-up; Ms. Rosa the librarian wears glasses) and short, rhythmic pages that are easy to read aloud
  • Ends with open ‘Talk about it’ prompts (a sign, a point or a tap on a talker counts too), a ‘Plan your own Play Day’ point-and-pick page and a free printable bonus for grown-ups

Questions

What ages is it for?

Ages 3–7. Younger siblings enjoy the refrain and the WOOF!, and older children can read the short pages themselves.

What’s inside?

A 32-page full-color story (12 spreads), ‘Talk about it’ prompts for grown-ups, a point-and-pick ‘Plan your own Play Day’ page and a QR code for a free printable planner and coloring pages.

Paperback or hardcover?

The paperback (8.5 × 8.5 in) is printed on demand by Amazon KDP. A case-laminate hardcover printed by IngramSpark may be added later.

Is this a book about screen rules?

No. It’s a funny story about a day of play. The tablet is a friendly, sleepy character, and Ada can’t wait to tell it about her day in the morning.

Is there a PDF?

No, the story is print only. The Play Day planner and coloring pages are a free download from the QR code in the book.

My child talks with a tablet or device (a talker). Is this book a good fit?

Yes. The sleepy tablet in the story is a made-up character, not a talker. The grown-up page says it plainly: a sign, a point or a tap on a talker counts, and a talker never takes a day off.

Is it a good gift?

Yes. It’s a funny read-aloud for ages 3–7 with a dedication page and a free printable planner to go with it. Order it with the recipient’s address and use the store’s gift options at checkout.

Is there a Spanish edition?

Not yet. The book already says to talk, sing and read in the language you know best, and the sounds (WOOF!, zzz-bip) work in any language.

How does a printed book reach me?

Each copy is printed when you order it and shipped by the printer, with tracking by email. The time to print and deliver is shown at checkout before you pay.

What can I do with it?

Use it with your own household, as often as you like. Please share a link to this page rather than the files. License terms

What if something is wrong?

Our shipping and returns page sets out exactly what happens if a file is broken, a book arrives damaged, or something isn’t as described.
